
-----------------

Introduction
============
We follow @ONeillRoberts-1999 in considering a data set obtained from a smallpox outbreak 
in a closed community of 120
individuals in Abakaliki, Nigeria [see @Bailey-1975, p. 125]. 
Removals are separated by the following 
interremoval times (measured in days, but with `0` adjusted to `ε > 0` in order to avoid coincidences).
Specific infectivity and removal rates are defined according to suggestions in @ONeillRoberts-1999
derived from a maximum likelihood analysis devised by Frank Ball.
```{julia}
#| label: initialization
population     = 120
ε              = 0.001 
interremovals  = [13, 7, 2, 3, ε, ε, 1, 4, 5, 3, 2, ε, 2, ε, 5, 3, 1, 4, ε, 1, 
                   1, 1, 2, ε, 1, 5, ε, 5, 5] 
α, β           = 0.0008, 0.088 
THRESHOLD      = length(interremovals) + 1 ;
cremoval_times = accumulate(+, interremovals) 
pushfirst!(cremoval_times, 0) 
duration = 10 + maximum(cremoval_times) ;
```
Note that the first `CRemoval` is deemed to have happened at time `0`.

We create maximal and minimal initial evolutions `evmin0` and `evmax0`, deriving from the most
minimal and maximal initial conditions possible,
under the reasonable assumption that all actual removals have been observed  as `CRemoval`s by time `{julia} duration`,
when our plots end,
(This considerably speeds up the simulation.)
```{julia}
#| label: setting up extremal evolutions
initial     = SIR(0, population - 1, 1, 0)
initial_min = SIR(0, population - 1, 1, 0)
initial_max = SIR(0, population - THRESHOLD, THRESHOLD, 0)

evmin0 = extremal_evolution(initial_min, duration, cremoval_times, 
    maximal=false) ;
evmax0 = extremal_evolution(initial_max, duration, cremoval_times, 
    maximal=true, all_cremovals_observed=true) ;
```
Plot `duration =` `{julia} duration` is set at `{julia} duration - maximum(cremoval_times)` days after the final removal,
a choice based on purely photogenic reasons.

The random `seed!` is fixed, in order to ensure repeatability.
```{julia}
#| label: initializing random seed
seed!(6) ;
```

Tabular and graphical displays of epidemics
===========================================
Here are some rather unimportant details about construction of plots,
which in due course may be incorporated in the module `EpidemicsUtilities` 
in a more generalized form. In particular it is convenient to import from `EpidemicsUtilities` some constants 
used for the plotting parameter `select`, namely
```{julia}
#| label: imports from `EpidemicsUtilities`
import EpidemicsUtilities: ACTIVATED, BOUNDARIES, ELEMENTS, LFET, NFZ
```

Here are specialized colours used in the plots.
```{julia}
#| label: choice of colours
min_spectrum    = [colorant"red"] 
append!(min_spectrum, range(colorant"grey5",   stop=colorant"grey99", length=11)) 
max_spectrum    = [colorant"blue"] 
append!(max_spectrum, range(colorant"grey5", stop=colorant"grey99",   length=11)) 
joined_colour   = colorant"deeppink" 
coalesce_colour = colorant"black" ;
```

Here are some more plotting technicalities.
```{julia}
#| label: basic graphics
uflow = table_trajectories1(duration, evmin0.trajectory) 
axes_plot = plot(uflow, 
    yintercept=0:5:THRESHOLD,
    Geom.hline(style=:dash, size=0.1mm, color=theme.scaffold),
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0-0.1, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=THRESHOLD + 0.25),
    Guide.yticks(ticks=0:10:THRESHOLD),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    style(default_color=theme.background),
    Theme(
        panel_fill=theme.blank,
        default_color=theme.default,
        background_color=theme.background,
        major_label_font="CMU Serif",   minor_label_font="CMU Serif",
        minor_label_color=theme.legend, major_label_color=theme.legend,
        major_label_font_size=6pt,     minor_label_font_size=4pt,
        plot_padding = [4pt, 2pt, 4pt, 4pt],
        grid_line_width=0mm,
)) 

push!(axes_plot, layer(uflow, x=:t, y=:empty, Geom.line,
    style(line_width=theme.trail, default_color=theme.scaffold))) 

lines_plot = new_figure(axes_plot,
    Scale.y_continuous(labels=(initial.n ≤ EpidemicsUtilities.MAXPOP ?
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_circled(i; n=initial.n) :
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_bracketed(i; n=initial.n))),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines")) ;
```



Implementation
==============
We have assumed the first observed removal to happen at time zero, and
we further assume a Bayesian prior distribution for the numbers of infectives at this time
which is uniform over the range of possibilities assuming that no removals take place after the
last `CRemoval` (and therefore that no infectives survive beyond this time!).
This is unduly pessimistic: it should be possible to _compute_ the prior distribution
given α and β.
```{julia}
#| label: setup simulation                                                                                                                                                                                                    
min_cremovals = [CRemoval(t, n) for (n, t) in enumerate(cremoval_times)]                                                                                                                                                          
iv_null  = CInnovation(initial.n, Infection[], Removal[], min_cremovals) 
threshold = THRESHOLD 
@test threshold == length(cremoval_times) ; # This test could be removed now!
```

Here is an operator which allows us succinctly to propose a change in the initial condition
for a `CEvolution`, which will be accepted only if it leads to a valid `CEvolution`.
Eventually this will be included in the module `EpidemicsCFTP` --
at present its employment corresponds to an independence sampler move
though it should be possible to vary this to be a simple Random Walk Metropolis
sampler (_simple RWM_).
In general, care needs to be taken that monotonicity is maintained!
[A similar situation is discussed in @KendallMoeller-2000.]
```{julia}
#| label: operators
"""
    ▷(::CEvolution, ::SIR) ::CEvolution (Use `\\diamond`.)

The succinct statement `cev ⋄ sir` checks whether one can replace
`cev.initial` by `sir` (but using time `cev.initial.t`). 
If so, then the resulting `CEvolution` is returned. 
If not, then the original `CEvolution` is returned.
### Example
{jldoctest}
cev = extremal_evolution(SIR(0, 1, 1, 0), 2.0, [1.0])
sir = SIR(0, 2, 0, 0)
cev ▷ sir

# output
CEvolution(SIR₀.₀₀(1:1:0),
infections: AbstractInfection[ℐ₀.₀₀¹⁻²]
removals:   AbstractRemoval[]
cremovals:  CRemoval[𝒞₁.₀₀²]
chronology: AbstractIncident[ℐ₀.₀₀¹⁻²,𝒞₁.₀₀²]
trajectory: SIR[SIR₀.₀₀(1:1:0),SIR₀.₀₀(0:2:0),SIR₁.₀₀(0:1:1)]
history:    AbstractIncident[ℐ₀.₀₀¹⁻²,𝒞₁.₀₀²])

"""
function ▷(cev::CEvolution, sir::SIR)::CEvolution
    try
        new_cev = CEvolution(sir, cev.chronology)
        return new_cev
    catch e
        if !((e isa EmployedRemoval) || (e isa MissedCRemoval))
            rethrow()
        end
        return cev
    end
end

"""
    proposed_sir(::SIR, ::Int)

Returns a modification of its first argument such that
the `i` field equals the second argument.
"""
function proposed_sir(sir, proposed_i)
    return SIR(sir.t, sir.s - (proposed_i - sir.i), proposed_i, sir.r)
end ;
```

The function `innovation_stream` supplies a single stream of tuples each giving
an `Innovation` and a proposal to change initial condition.
For now we simply ensure this is long enough to fuel the entire CFTP process,
though in principle it would be easy to extend this as required!
```{julia}
#| label: function `innovation_stream`
function innovation_stream(cycle_length; 
    evmin=evmin0, iv_null=iv_null, duration=duration, α=α, β=β, threshold=threshold)
    stream = []
    for iteration ∈ 1:cycle_length
        # `Innovation`
        iv    = generate_innovation(iv_null, duration; α=α, β=β, threshold=threshold)
        # Proposed initial infection level
        proposed_i = rand(Distributions.DiscreteUniform(1, threshold - evmin.initial.r))
        push!(stream, (iv, proposed_i))
    end
    return stream
end ;
```

A function `single_frame` updates minimal and maximal `CEvolution`s by a single algorithmic step.
Note that we vary the initial number of infectives using a separate accept/reject step
in the update.
```{julia}
#| label: function `single_frame`
function single_frame(work, evmin, evmax, iv, proposed_i; duration=duration, theme=theme)
    evmin = evmin ⋄ iv ▷ proposed_sir(evmin.initial, proposed_i) ;
    evmax = evmax ⋄ iv ▷ proposed_sir(evmax.initial, proposed_i) ;
    
    # Omit next conditional statement once thoroughly tested!
    if !(evmin ⪯ evmax)
        error("Monotonicity fails")
    end

    if evmin ≃ evmax
        draw_evolution!(work, evmin, duration, theme=theme, 
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=coalesce_colour)
    else
        draw_evolution!(work, evmin, duration, theme=theme, 
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=min_spectrum[1])
        draw_evolution!(work, evmax, duration, theme=theme,
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=max_spectrum[1])
    end

    return evmin, evmax
end ;
```

Most of the work of the CFTP algorithm will be done by the `cycle` function.
Note that previous cycles are included in the plots as relevant. Ideally we should plot
these as greyed out, but this is a matter for later.
```{julia}
#| label: function `cycle`
function cycle(stream, canvas; 
        evmin0=evmin0, evmax0=evmax0, tag="demo-f", lines_plot=lines_plot, theme=theme)
    work = deepcopy(lines_plot)
    evmin = deepcopy(evmin0)
    evmax = deepcopy(evmax0)
    iteration = 0
    legend  = lpad(iteration, 4, "0")
    legend2 = "-$(lpad(length(stream)-iteration, 4, "0"))"
    draw_evolution!(work, evmin, duration, theme=theme,
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=min_spectrum[1])
    draw_evolution!(work, evmax, duration, theme=theme,
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=max_spectrum[1])
    title = "Minimum and maximum evolutions at algorithmic time step $legend2"
    image = new_figure(work; title=title)
    draw(PNG("animation/demo-$tag-$legend.png"), image)
    draw(PDF("animation/demo-$tag-$legend.pdf"), image)

    for (iteration, pair) ∈ enumerate(stream)
        #(work, evmin, evmax) = single_frame(evmin, evmax, pair...)
        (evmin, evmax) = single_frame(canvas[iteration], evmin, evmax, pair...)
        
        legend = lpad(iteration, 4, "0")
        legend2 = "-$(lpad(length(stream)-iteration, 4, "0"))"
        coalesced = (evmin ≃ evmax) ? "[COALESCED]" : ""
        title="Minimum and maximum evolutions at algorithmic time step $legend2 $coalesced"
        
        image = new_figure(canvas[iteration]; title=title)
        draw(PNG("animation/$tag-$legend.png"), image)
        if mod(iteration, 10) == 0
            draw(PDF("animation/$tag-$legend.pdf"), image)
        end
    end
end ;
```

This code is used to plot an entire CFTP sequence of sequences of updates in algorithmic time: see [Appendix @sec-figures].
I suspect that considerable speed-up could be achieved by _not_ plotting each frame of each cycle!

Graphical illustration of CFTP {#sec-figures}
==============================

In this appendix we display an entire evolution of a CFTP run, always starting with minimal and maximal evolutions
`evmin0` and `evmax0` given above. 
An [animated `GIF`](file:///home/wilfrid/ms/PerfectEpidemics/julia/animation-demo.gif) displays the entire CFTP,
evolving in logical time and re-starting earlier and earlier till coalescence is achieved!

There follow a selection of figures illustrating the final cycle of the CFTP algorithm, 
sampled at every ten steps from step `10` onwards up to step `250` and also displaying runs of previous cycles
where appropriate. 
The work of each CFTP cycle is carried out by the function `cycle`. Note that we have not yet automated 
how CFTP works through cycles.
```{julia}
#| label: building figures
max_length = 256
stream = innovation_stream(max_length)
canvas = [deepcopy(lines_plot) for iteration ∈ 1:max_length]

for (epithet, cycle_length) ∈ [("a", 8), ("b", 16), ("c", 32), ("d", 64), ("e", 128), ("f", 256),]
    cycle(stream[max_length - cycle_length + 1:max_length], 
        canvas[max_length - cycle_length + 1:max_length], 
        tag="demo-$epithet")
end
```

Now we create a `GIF` of the entire CFTP run, working with `ImageMagick` on the command-line.
(Construction might be quicker if run in memory!)
```{julia}
#| label: creating GIF using CLI
lexicon = ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"]
for epithet ∈ lexicon
    run(`convert -delay 15 animation/demo-$epithet-\*.png -layers Optimize animation-demo-$epithet.gif`)
end
intermediates = [("-delay", "50", "animation/demo-$epithet-0001.png", "-delay", "5",
                    "animation-demo-$epithet.gif") for epithet ∈ lexicon]
sequence = collect(Iterators.flatten(intermediates))
run(`convert -loop 1 $sequence -layers Optimize animation-demo.gif`)
run(`rm $(["animation-demo-$epithet.gif" for epithet in lexicon])`) ;
```
We start with the initial configuration of maximal and minimal evolutions at time `0`,
and then plot continuation of the final CFTP cycle. Note that it would be helpful to
display times as _negative_ terminating at time `0`!

It would also be better to display previous cycles as greyed out. Note however that it 
would be immediately visually apparent if sandwiching were to fail!
